title: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine as Monsoon Season Drives Fresh Outbreaks
excerpt: Takeda's QDENGA, approved for ages 4 to 60, can be administered regardless of prior dengue infection — a key advantage over earlier vaccine candidates that stalled in the Indian market.
body:
• India's drug regulator approved QDENGA, the country's first dengue vaccine, for people aged 4 to 60
  • Unlike Sanofi's Dengvaxia, QDENGA can be given regardless of prior dengue infection and requires no pre-screening
  • The vaccine showed 80.2% efficacy against confirmed dengue and 90.4% efficacy against hospitalization in clinical trials
  • The vaccine will initially be imported from Germany, with Indian manufacturing planned through a partnership with Biological E

India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation has granted marketing authorisation to QDENGA, making it the first dengue vaccine approved in the country. The vaccine, developed by Japan's Takeda Biopharmaceuticals, is cleared for use in individuals aged 4 to 60 years.

The approval comes as India enters peak dengue season, with outbreaks reported across multiple states during the annual monsoon. All four dengue virus serotypes are known to circulate simultaneously in several Indian regions, making the disease a persistent public health challenge.

How It Works

QDENGA is a live-attenuated vaccine that protects against all four dengue virus serotypes. It is administered as two 0.5 ml doses given three months apart via subcutaneous injection.

A critical advantage is that QDENGA can be given to people regardless of whether they have previously been infected with dengue, eliminating the need for pre-vaccination blood testing. This sets it apart from Sanofi's Dengvaxia, which is recommended only for people with a prior infection due to concerns that it could worsen outcomes in dengue-naive individuals. Dengvaxia has not been approved in India, according to Reuters.

In its pivotal Phase III trial involving over 20,000 participants across eight countries, QDENGA demonstrated 80.2% efficacy against virologically confirmed dengue at 12 months after the second dose. At 18 months, it showed 90.4% efficacy against dengue-related hospitalization, according to Takeda.

When Will It Be Available?

While the marketing authorisation has been granted, the vaccine is not expected to be available in India until the first half of 2027, as several regulatory steps involving imports remain, according to Peter Streibl, Takeda's General Manager for Southeast Asia and India.

The vaccine will initially be imported from Germany. Pricing and availability details will be announced once local processes are complete, Streibl told The Hindu BusinessLine.

For longer-term supply, Takeda has partnered with Hyderabad-based Biological E to manufacture QDENGA in India. Under the Make in India initiative, local production is expected to ensure faster supply and potentially lower costs. Multidose vials for government procurement in endemic countries are planned by 2030.

The Dengue Burden

India is among the countries with the highest dengue burden globally. The disease, spread by Aedes mosquitoes, causes symptoms ranging from high fever and severe body aches to life-threatening complications requiring hospitalisation. Peak transmission coincides with the monsoon season from June through October.

"India carries a substantial dengue burden, and all four dengue virus serotypes have been documented as co-circulating in several regions. QDENGA is designed to protect against all four serotypes, regardless of prior exposure."

— Dr. Goh Choo Beng, Takeda Medical Affairs Head for Southeast Asia and India

Experts have cautioned that while the vaccine can reduce severe disease and hospitalization, it is unlikely to prevent outbreaks as long as mosquito transmission continues. Dr. Divya K.S. of Apollo Hospitals told Reuters that the vaccine should be seen as one component of a broader strategy that includes vector control, surveillance, and public awareness.

What NRIs Should Know

For members of the Indian diaspora who travel to India during monsoon months to visit family, dengue has long been a serious concern. The vaccine could eventually offer a preventive option for travelers heading to endemic regions, though availability and pricing for the Indian private market remain to be clarified.

Meanwhile, Hyderabad-based Indian Immunologicals is developing its own dengue vaccine candidate and is preparing to begin mid-stage clinical trials, according to Reuters. QDENGA has already been approved in 43 countries, with more than 24 million doses distributed globally since its launch in 2022.
